question:
(a) Explain the effect of forward bias on a $p\text{-}n$ junction.
(b) Explain the effect of reverse bias on the depletion region and current through the junction.

options.A:
(a) Forward bias increases the potential barrier and widens depletion region, so almost no current flows.
(b) Reverse bias reduces barrier and gives a large majority-carrier current.
options.B:
(a) Forward bias and reverse bias both leave the depletion layer unchanged.
(b) Current is always same in both conditions.
options.C:
(a) Forward bias makes holes move n-to-p and electrons p-to-n, increasing the barrier.
(b) Reverse bias gives a large current due to majority carriers.
options.D:
(a) In forward bias, p-side is connected to positive and n-side to negative. The applied voltage opposes the barrier, narrows the depletion layer and lets majority carriers cross, producing large current.
(b) In reverse bias, p-side is connected to negative and n-side to positive. The barrier and depletion width increase, majority carriers move away from the junction, and only a small minority-carrier reverse saturation current flows.
